status_summary: Sunset provisions are operative for some energy regulators and no commission was found. Executive Order 14270 (signed 2025-04-09, 90 FR 15643) directs EPA, DOE, FERC, NRC and certain Interior and Army Corps components to add conditional sunset dates to covered existing regulations and to give new covered rules sunset dates no more than five years out; FERC published a direct final rule on 2025-10-21 (90 FR 48397), effective 2025-12-05, under which 53 listed regulations cease to have effect on 2026-12-05 unless extended (a correcting amendment of 2026-02-06, 91 FR 5290, fixed an error in that rule), and the NRC published a direct final rule on 2025-12-03 (90 FR 55621) whose effective date of 2026-01-08 it confirmed on 2026-01-08 (91 FR 553), withdrawing one amendment, with listed provisions sunsetting one year after the rule took effect unless extended. On 2026-04-08 the NRC published a final rule (91 FR 17757) adding a sunset date of 2027-04-08 to the aircraft impact assessment section it had withdrawn from the earlier rule. DOE published a direct final rule on 2026-05-29 (91 FR 31869) adding conditional sunset dates to 28 parts of its regulations, then withdrew it on 2026-07-09 (91 FR 42337) after adverse comments, leaving its companion proposed rule of 2026-05-29 (91 FR 31985) as the route. Executive Orders 14192 (ten-for-one repeal) and 14219 (review of all regulations) do not provide sunsets or a commission, and no presidentially appointed Regulatory Reduction Commission or annual repeal package to Congress was found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14270 (signed 2025-04-09) on zero-based regulatory budgeting with conditional sunset dates was published.
FERC published a direct final rule (90 FR 48397), effective 2025-12-05, adding a conditional sunset date of 2026-12-05 to 53 regulations.
NRC published a direct final rule adding conditional sunset dates to listed regulations, effective 2026-01-08 unless significant adverse comments were received.
NRC confirmed the 2026-01-08 effective date of its sunset rule (91 FR 553), withdrawing the amendment that would have added a sunset date to 10 CFR 50.150 on aircraft impact assessment.

FERC publishes a correcting amendment (91 FR 5290, FR Doc. 2026-02431, effective 2026-02-06) fixing an error in its 2025-10-21 direct final rule that added a conditional sunset date to certain regulations in 18 CFR part 157, issued under Executive Order 14270.

NRC published a final rule (91 FR 17757, effective 2026-04-08) adding a sunsetting paragraph to the aircraft impact assessment requirements in 10 CFR 50.150, after withdrawing that amendment from its direct final rule on significant adverse comments and responding to comments on the companion proposed rule of 2025-12-03 (90 FR 55699); the section ceases to have effect on 2027-04-08 unless extended.

DOE published a direct final rule (91 FR 31869, Docket DOE-HQ-2025-0603) under Executive Order 14270 adding conditional sunset dates to 28 existing parts of 10 CFR (2027-07-13 for 21 parts, 2031-07-13 for seven parts), with a companion proposed rule published the same day.

DOE withdrew its 2026-05-29 direct final rule (91 FR 42337) because it received adverse comments, before the stated effective date of 2026-07-13; the companion proposed rule (91 FR 31985) remains the basis for any final action.

title: Ease trade adjustment with regulatory sunsets and a Regulatory Reduction Commission
uncertainties: The status of the DOE companion proposed rule (published 2026-05-29) after the withdrawal was not retrieved. Federal Register API queries through 2026-11-02 did not surface EPA, Interior or Army Corps sunset rules, and a search of that rulemaking did not identify one in the Federal Register; a blog report (unverified lead, chemical-facility-security-news host) said an EPA sunset final rule went to OMB in November 2025. Whether the FERC rule took effect without significant adverse comment was not confirmed beyond a later partial rescission notice effective 2026-01-20 seen in search results. The count of 53 FERC regulations is taken from the rule's own statement and could not be reproduced exactly from its table of contents. A further NRC notice of 2026-02-03 (FR Doc. 2026-02165), described as a confirmation with a correction, was not read, and the FERC correction of 2026-02-06 (FR Doc. 2026-02431) was read only through its Federal Register API summary, which does not say what the error was. Executive Orders 14192 and 14219 are context for deregulation, and the absence of a commission rests on searches and on Executive Order 14270 creating none. The match is partial because the sunsets cover regulations of named energy agencies, not new regulations generally, and are not framed as trade adjustment measures.
